name: Circuit de Monaco
summary: The slowest, tightest and most famous lap in Formula 1. Overtaking is mostly theoretical.
character: Barriers everywhere, no run-off and the shortest lap of the year. Qualifying decides most races, so Saturday is the big day. The tunnel is the fastest part of the lap, and drivers come out of it into bright daylight.

corners.name: Fairmont Hairpin
corners.note: The slowest corner in F1, at around 50 km/h. Full steering lock.

corners.name: Casino Square
corners.note: Uphill, blind and bumpy, past the casino. Get it wrong and the barrier is right there.

corners.name: Sainte Devote
corners.note: Turn 1, a tight right after the start. First-lap pile-ups are a tradition here.

corners.name: Tunnel and Nouvelle Chicane
corners.note: Flat out in the dark, then hard braking for the harbour chicane: the one real overtaking spot.

corners.name: Swimming Pool and La Rascasse
corners.note: A quick left-right round the pool, then a tight hairpin by the bar.

moments.title: Senna's pole by a second and a half
moments.body: Ayrton Senna took pole 1.4 seconds clear of his McLaren teammate Alain Prost and later said it felt as if he was driving on instinct alone. On Sunday he crashed out of the lead at Portier and walked home.

history.body: First Monaco Grand Prix, run by the Automobile Club de Monaco.
Part of the first World Championship season. It then dropped off the championship calendar until 1955.
Alberto Ascari crashed into the harbour and swam out.
The swimming pool section was added.
The only year the race hasn't run since 1955, because of the pandemic.
